new_inferences: The candidate skips the required shadow-read interval.
Row counts alone cannot satisfy the reconciliation gate; cent totals, checksums, and the published report are missing, while partial-refund checksum work remains open.
The duplicate observation cannot establish retry-worker safety while its cause and crash behavior remain unresolved.
The proposed Redis identifier map revives a superseded direction and leaves the missing timezone mappings unresolved.
Deferring the representative load test leaves the latency commitment unverified before cohort activation.
Deleting Ledger V2 rows violates the rollback decision and destructive-SQL constraint; delaying cache invalidation leaves the rollback ordering gap open.

blocking_findings.rationale: The proposed 25 percent cohort would begin Ledger V2 reads without the required shadow-read interval.

Matching row counts alone does not meet the row-count, cent-total, and checksum gate. Partial refunds are excluded despite an unfinished checksum formula, and the required pre-approval report is absent.
The retry-worker duplicate observation is unresolved, and crash-safe prevention of duplicate outbox rows has not been proved.
The two tenant timezone mappings remain unresolved. A Redis identifier map does not supply those mappings and revives a superseded identifier-map direction.
The representative release-candidate load test is deferred until after activation, leaving the p95 latency commitment unverified.
Deleting cohort Ledger V2 rows contradicts the preservation decision and the ban on destructive SQL. Cache invalidation ordering remains unresolved.
